title: Ports, Protocols and Services

header.html: 1.4 Explain common networking ports, protocols, services and traffic types: the port list; IP types (ICMP, TCP, UDP, GRE, IPsec with AH, ESP and IKE); traffic types (unicast, multicast, anycast, broadcast)
the official CompTIA Network+ N10-009 exam objectives, version 4.0

html:
1The port list to memorize

Protocol Port Notes
FTP (File Transfer Protocol) 20/21 Clear text; 21 control, 20 data
SFTP (Secure FTP) 22 Runs over SSH
SSH (Secure Shell) 22 Encrypted remote administration
Telnet 23 Clear text remote login (avoid)
SMTP 25 Sends mail between servers
DNS 53 Names to addresses, UDP and TCP
DHCP 67/68 67 server, 68 client, UDP
TFTP 69 Simple, unauthenticated file transfer, UDP
HTTP 80 Web, clear text
NTP 123 Time, UDP
SNMP 161/162 161 queries, 162 traps
LDAP 389 Directory access
HTTPS 443 Web over TLS
SMB 445 Windows file sharing
Syslog 514 Log messages, UDP
SMTPS 587 Secure mail submission
LDAPS 636 LDAP over SSL/TLS
SQL Server 1433 Microsoft SQL database
RDP 3389 Remote Desktop
SIP 5060/5061 Voice signaling; 5061 is encrypted

Exam tip

. Secure versions use different ports: SSH 22 (not Telnet 23), HTTPS 443 (not HTTP 80), LDAPS 636 (not LDAP 389). SSH, SFTP share port 22.

2IP types

Protocol Role
ICMP Error and diagnostic messages (ping, traceroute); no ports
TCP Reliable, connection-oriented: handshake, acknowledgements, retransmission, ordering
UDP Fast, connectionless, no guarantee (voice, DNS, streaming)
GRE (Generic Routing Encapsulation) Tunnels other protocols inside IP
IPsec Secures IP traffic: AH (Authentication Header: integrity and authentication, no encryption), ESP (Encapsulating Security Payload: encryption plus integrity), IKE (Internet Key Exchange: negotiates keys and security associations)
Exam tip

. TCP = reliable and slower; UDP = fast and unreliable. ESP encrypts; AH does not.

3Traffic types

Type Delivery
Unicast One sender to one receiver
Multicast One sender to a group that joined
Anycast One sender to the nearest of several receivers sharing an address
Broadcast One sender to every device on the local network

IPv6 has no broadcast; it uses multicast.

Exam tip

. Know the secure pairs: HTTP 80 and HTTPS 443, LDAP 389 and LDAPS 636, SMTP 25 and SMTPS 587, Telnet 23 and SSH 22.

4Exam Q&A

4.1 Practice questions (choose the best answer)

S1An administrator needs an encrypted remote command line to a switch. Which protocol and port fit?

  • ATelnet on port 23
  • BRDP on port 3389
  • CHTTP on port 80
  • DSSH on port 22
Show the answer

Answer: D. SSH provides encrypted remote administration on port 22.

S2A web server must allow secure browsing. Which port should the firewall allow?

  • A80
  • B53
  • C445
  • D443
Show the answer

Answer: D. HTTPS uses port 443.

S3Which protocol uses ports 161 and 162?

  • ANTP
  • BSyslog
  • CSNMP
  • DDHCP
Show the answer

Answer: C. SNMP uses 161 for queries and 162 for traps.

S4Which IPsec component provides encryption of the payload?

  • AAH
  • BIKE
  • CGRE
  • DESP
Show the answer

Answer: D. ESP encrypts; AH only authenticates.

S5Traffic is delivered to the closest of several servers that share one IP address. Which traffic type is this?

  • AMulticast
  • BBroadcast
  • CUnicast
  • DAnycast
Show the answer

Answer: D. Anycast delivers to the nearest member.

S6Which transport protocol is best for real-time voice where speed matters more than retransmission?

  • ATCP
  • BICMP
  • CUDP
  • DGRE
Show the answer

Answer: C. UDP is fast and connectionless.

4.2 Recall questions

R1Which port does DNS use?

Show the answer

53.

R2Which ports does DHCP use?

Show the answer

67 (server) and 68 (client).

R3Which port does RDP use?

Show the answer

3389.

R4What does IKE do?

Show the answer

Negotiates keys and security associations for IPsec.

R5Is there broadcast in IPv6?

Show the answer

No, IPv6 uses multicast.

R6Which protocol uses port 389, and which secure version uses 636?

Show the answer

LDAP (389) and LDAPS (636).

5Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
Remote SSH 22, Telnet 23, RDP 3389
Web and mail HTTP 80, HTTPS 443, SMTP 25, SMTPS 587
Infrastructure DNS 53, DHCP 67/68, NTP 123, SNMP 161/162, Syslog 514, TFTP 69
Files and directories FTP 20/21, SFTP 22, SMB 445, LDAP 389, LDAPS 636
Traffic unicast, multicast, anycast, broadcast
IPsec AH (no encryption), ESP (encrypts), IKE (keys)
